title: Helios Technologies’ Electronics Segment Expands Support Across Briggs & Stratton Ecosystem
summary: SARASOTA, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Helios Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: HLIO) (“Helios” or the “Company”), a global leader in highly…...
body_text: Helios Technologies’ Electronics Segment Expands Support Across Briggs & Stratton Ecosystem July 14, 2026 9:00am EDT Download as PDF SARASOTA, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Helios Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: HLIO) (“Helios” or the “Company”), a global leader in highly engineered motion control and electronic controls technology, today announced that two businesses within its Electronics Segment— i3 Product Development (“i3PD”) and Enovation Controls (“Enovation”)—are supporting the off-highway equipment industry through separate commercial relationships with Briggs & Stratton . While each relationship serves a distinct role, together they highlight the breadth of engineering, systems integration, and electronic control capabilities available across the Helios Electronics Segment. i3PD recently joined the Briggs & Stratton Vanguard™ Battery Technology Partner program , where it provides product design, engineering, and systems integration services for OEMs adopting Vanguard commercial battery technology. "We are thrilled to welcome i3 Product Development to our growing network of Vanguard Battery Technology Partners," said David Frank, Senior Vice President and President of Electrification at Briggs & Stratton. "By combining our proven battery technology with i3PD’s expertise in complex system integration, we can help OEMs confidently navigate the transition to electrified equipment." In addition, Enovation continues its supplier relationship with Ferris®, a Briggs & Stratton company, providing products including the PV485 display and IX3212 Power Distribution Module for commercial equipment applications. "These relationships demonstrate the diverse capabilities within our Electronics Segment," said Billy Aldridge, President, Electronics of Helios. "Whether through engineering services at i3PD or electronic control solutions from Enovation, our businesses create value for customers at different stages of product development and production. Together, they reflect the depth of expertise and customer-focused solutions we bring to the off-highway equipment market." About Briggs & Stratton Briggs & Stratton, headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, provides innovative products and diverse power solutions to help people get work done. Briggs & Stratton is the world’s largest producer of engines for lawn and garden, turf care and job site power equipment and is a leading designer, manufacturer and marketer of lithium-ion batteries, standby generators and energy storage systems through its Briggs & Stratton®, Vanguard®, Ferris®, Simplicity®, Snapper®, Billy Goat® and Branco® brands. Briggs & Stratton products are designed, manufactured, marketed and serviced in over 100 countries on six continents. Learn more at BriggsandStratton.com . About i3 Product Development i3 Product Development is a full-service product development firm that partners with leading manufacturers to design, engineer, and deliver innovative products. With expertise spanning mechanical and electrical engineering, industrial and UI/UX design, embedded systems, software development, and rapid prototyping, i3PD helps bring complex products to market with a focus on performance, reliability, and manufacturability. Learn more at i3pd.com and follow us on LinkedIn . About Enovation Controls Enovation Controls is a fast-growing and innovative manufacturer of electronic controls and displays for diverse markets. As an international leader in fully tailored solutions, Enovation Controls offers a broad range of displays, controls, and instrumentation products for various applications. With an internationally diverse team, we serve customers around the world through our global sales, manufacturing, and engineering operations. Enovation Controls partners directly with OEMs and supports a worldwide network of authorized distributors and system integrators. Visit us at www.enovationcontrols.com and follow us on LinkedIn . About Helios Technologies Helios Technologies is a global leader in highly engineered motion control and electronic controls technology, providing premium products that ensure safety, reliability, and seamless connectivity to diverse end markets including agriculture, construction, data centers, energy, health and wellness, industrial, marine, material handling, and recreational vehicles. Helios sells its products to customers in over 80 countries around the world. Its strategy is to be a diversified, customer-centric global enterprise distinguished by innovation, operational speed, and a high-performance culture. The Company has paid a cash dividend to its shareholders every quarter since becoming a public company in 1997. For more information please visit: www.heliostechnologies.com and follow us on LinkedIn . View source version on businesswire.com: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260714015992/en/ Product/Solutions contact: Kati Zumwalt Director, Marketing – Electronics Segment (918) 317-4100 kati.zumwalt@enovationcontrols.com Investor and Media contacts: Tania Almond Vice President, Investor Relations and Corporate Communication (941) 362-1333 tania.almond@HLIO.com Deborah Pawlowski Alliance Advisors LLC (716) 843-3908 dpawlowski@allianceadvisors.com Source: Helios Technologies, Inc. Released July 14, 2026

title: eCommerce email marketing: Strategies, types, and examples
summary: eCommerce email marketing drives sales, recovers carts, and builds loyalty. See the email types, campaign strategies, and examples that work across channels.
body_text: eCommerce email marketing is using email to promote products, recover lost sales, and build loyalty for an online store across the entire customer journey. It's one of the few channels you actually own. No social algorithm decides who sees your message, the list is yours, and it reliably returns more than it costs to run. This guide covers what eCommerce email marketing is, the email types worth sending, the strategies that lift revenue, how AI sharpens them, and real examples to borrow from. Throughout, you'll see why email performs best when you coordinate it with push, SMS, and in-app, and personalize it per shopper, rather than firing it off on its own. TL;DR eCommerce email marketing spans the full customer journey, from welcome and promotional campaigns to abandoned cart recovery, transactional messages, and post-purchase follow-ups. It's a direct, owned channel, so you reach customers without paying an algorithm for access, which makes retention-focused email some of the most cost-efficient revenue you have. A strong program mixes automated triggers, like welcome, cart recovery, and post-purchase, with scheduled campaigns, like promotions and seasonal sends. Email works hardest coordinated with push, SMS, and in-app under one customer profile, with frequency capping that keeps people from feeling swamped. AI adds two things: generative AI that creates content, subject lines, and image variations, and individual-level decisioning that picks the right message and send time for each customer. What is eCommerce email marketing? eCommerce email marketing is the practice of using email to drive sales, recover revenue, and build loyalty for an online store. It works across the customer journey, spanning acquisition, conversion, and retention. It blends automated triggered messages, like welcome, cart recovery, and post-purchase, with scheduled campaigns, like promotions and seasonal sends. Automated and scheduled emails An eCommerce email program runs on two types of send. Automated messages fire when a shopper takes an action, and scheduled campaigns go out on a calendar you set. Automated, or triggered, emails react to behavior in real time. A signup prompts a welcome email, an abandoned cart starts a recovery sequence, and a purchase fires a transactional email, then post-purchase follow-ups. These run on marketing automation, so they send without anyone hitting the button. Scheduled campaigns are the sends you plan and time yourself, like a product launch, a seasonal sale, or a monthly newsletter. You pick the audience and the moment. A direct channel you own Email is a direct line to your customers that no outside platform controls. You own the list, you decide what goes out, and your message reaches the inbox without an algorithm ranking it or charging you for reach. This separates email from rented channels like paid social and search ads, where visibility depends on a bidding system or a feed algorithm you don't control. The relationship sits between you and a subscriber who chose to hear from you, a steadier base to build repeat revenue on. Why email marketing matters for eCommerce Email matters for eCommerce because it's a direct channel you own, and it lifts results across acquisition, conversion, and retention. You aren't renting reach from a platform that can change its algorithm or its ad prices overnight. You're talking to people who asked to hear from you. Among retail and eCommerce , email is the favored engagement channel at 43%, ahead of messaging apps at 39% and SMS at 38%, according to the Retail Customer Engagement Review . It's also a channel brands keep funding, with global email marketing revenue reaching around $9.5 billion in 2024 and climbing since. Email marketing for online stores across the funnel Email works at all three stages of the shopping journey, covering acquisition, conversion, and retention through a single subscriber relationship. When email is in the mix, Braze research found shoppers are 89% more likely to purchase than those reached only on other channels, a real lift at the conversion stage rather than added awareness. Here's how the work splits across the funnel: Acquisition. A welcome series turns a new subscriber into a first-time buyer, often with an introductory offer to get the first purchase over the line. Conversion. Cart reminders, product recommendations, and well-timed promotions move hesitant shoppers toward checkout. Retention. Post-purchase follow-ups, loyalty rewards, and win-back sends bring existing customers back for the next order. Why retention makes email compound Retention is where email pays off hardest, because keeping a customer costs far less than winning a new one. The same shoppers show 81% longer average lifetimes when email is part of how they're reached. Since you own the channel, that added value arrives without the rising per-acquisition costs that paid channels carry, so returns accrue instead of resetting with every campaign. Handle retention this way and email becomes the engine of your lifecycle marketing, turning one-time buyers into a base of repeat revenue you can forecast. Types of eCommerce emails to send A complete eCommerce email marketing program leans on seven core types: welcome, transactional and post-purchase, abandoned cart, product recommendation, re-engagement and win-back, loyalty and rewards, and promotional and seasonal. Each is built for a different point in the customer's journey. Here's what each one does, when to send it, and what it's good for. Best for: Welcome series The first messages a new subscriber receives, sent right after they opt in. Engagement runs highest in those opening days, so a short welcome series is your best shot at turning fresh interest into a first order. Our roundup of the best welcome campaigns has examples worth stealing. Best for: Transactional and post-purchase emails A transactional email confirms an order, then shipping and delivery updates follow. People actively want these, so open rates run high, which makes them prime space for a loyalty nudge or a related-product suggestion once the essential info is covered. Best for: Abandoned cart emails Triggered when a shopper adds items but leaves before paying, usually as a short sequence rather than a single send. They're the highest-value trigger in eCommerce, because the shopper already showed intent. Our guide to abandoned cart recovery covers the timing, incentives, and flows in full. Best for: Product recommendation emails Personalized picks based on what a shopper browsed or bought, sent on a cadence or triggered by behavior. They work because relevance beats volume, a suggestion tied to real interest earns the click. Best for: Re-engagement and win-back emails Messages aimed at subscribers who've gone quiet, sent after a set stretch of inactivity. Reviving a lapsed customer costs far less than acquiring a new one, so even a modest recovery rate pays for itself. Best for: Loyalty and rewards emails Points updates, VIP perks, and birthday gifts sent to your loyalty segments or triggered by milestones. They make your best customers feel recognized, which nudges repeat purchases. Best for: Promotional and seasonal emails Scheduled sales, launches, and holiday campaigns timed to your calendar and to peak shopping moments. They drive volume and urgency, and they capitalize on high-intent windows like Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Examples of high-impact eCommerce email campaign strategies Here are eight high-impact eCommerce email campaign strategies that work to build relationships, relevance, and revenue: Personalized product recommendations. Use browse and purchase history to suggest what a shopper is likely to want next. Relevance drives the click, so you convert without leaning on a markdown. VIP and exclusive access. Give your best customers early access to launches and sales before anyone else. Exclusivity rewards loyalty and creates urgency without cutting the price. Back-in-stock and price-drop alerts. Tell shoppers when a sold-out item returns or a watched item gets cheaper. These reach people who already raised their hand, so intent runs high and conversion follows. First-purchase incentives. Give new subscribers a reason to place that first order, usually a small welcome discount or free shipping. This targets the one moment a discount actually pays for itself, turning a browser into a buyer. Win-back campaigns. Reach lapsed customers with a reminder of what they liked or a reason to come back. It costs far less than acquisition, and their history tells you exactly what to put in front of them. Referral and give-get. Reward existing customers for bringing friends, with both sides getting something. A recommendation from someone trusted converts better than any ad you could run. Milestone and anniversary. Mark a birthday or the anniversary of a first order with a note and maybe a perk. These land because they center on the customer rather than the sale. Social proof and UGC. Feature reviews, ratings, and real customer photos in your campaigns. Seeing genuine buyers reassures the hesitant ones and does the persuading for you. Why eCommerce email works best cross-channel The highest-performing eCommerce email programs coordinate with push, SMS, and in-app rather than running email in a silo. If you work from one unified customer profile, the channels reinforce each other. For example, you could have cart recovery messages sent across email and SMS , back-in-stock alerts via push, and promotions on the channel each customer responds to best, all sent at the time that suits that customer too. Run channels in silos and the shopper could receive all of those messages at once. With no frequency capping or consistency, the messages lose their relevance and create fatigue, no matter how good the content or the offer. Cross-channel orchestration solves that, with one profile, one coordinated cadence across everything you send. How AI improves eCommerce email marketing AI improves eCommerce email marketing in two distinct ways. Generative AI creates the content. AI decisioning works out what to send each customer and when. Generative AI for content and subject lines Generative AI drafts email copy, produces subject-line variants, and generates image variations far faster than a person building each from scratch. Feed it a brief and it returns several options to test, which keeps campaigns fresh as your subscriber base grows. It speeds up production of all your content, but you still edit, approve, and set the brand voice. AI decisioning for what to send and when AI decisioning handles the choices generative AI can't, picking the right message, offer, and moment for each individual person based on how they behave. It personalizes product recommendations, chooses the message most likely to drive the customer forward, and optimizes send time per person rather than blasting the whole list at 9 a.m. This individual-level decisioning is action optimization. BrazeAI Decisioning Studio™ does exactly this, making 1:1 decisions that optimize any business KPI you set, whether that's revenue, retention, or repeat purchase rate. Pair it with generative AI and you get relevant content delivered to the right person at the right moment, without a marketer hand-picking every send. How to build your eCommerce email marketing strategy (and measure it) To build an eCommerce email marketing strategy, follow these email marketing best practices . Pick a goal, work out who it's for, set your core sends to run on their own, then watch what comes back and adjust. The framework below runs in three stages, then covers the numbers that tell you it's working and the mistakes that stop most programs from growing. Stage 1: Set objectives and segment your audience Start with what you're trying to move and who you're talking to. Everything downstream depends on these two. Set clear objectives. Tie each campaign to a business outcome, more first orders, a higher repeat rate, fewer lapsed customers. The objective decides what you measure later. Segment your audience. Split your list by behavior, purchase history, and lifecycle stage so each message lands relevant. Strong segmentation runs on first-party data, the browsing, buying, and preference signals shoppers hand you directly. Stage 2: Use eCommerce email automation for your core sequences With goals and segments set, put automation to work. Build the triggered sequences that carry the most weight, then let them run on their own. Welcome series greets new subscribers while interest is highest. Cart recovery chases near-misses before intent fades. Post-purchase follows up with recent buyers. Win-back re-engages the ones going quiet. Marketing automation handles the timing on all four, so each fires the moment it's relevant instead of on your next send date. Stage 3: Sharpen and protect every send Good sequences still need sharp craft and a clean list behind them. This stage keeps your emails landing and your program healthy. Write subject lines and CTAs that earn the click. Keep subject lines short and specific, and give every email one clear call to action rather than three competing ones. Optimize for mobile. Most shoppers open on a phone, so single-column layouts, short copy, and tappable buttons aren't optional. Keep your list clean and compliant. Prune inactive subscribers to protect deliverability, use confirmed opt-ins, and follow the rules that apply to you, like GDPR and CAN-SPAM. Stage 4: Measure what matters Measure eCommerce email marketing success with a handful of metrics: open rate, click-through rate, conversion rate, revenue per email, unsubscribe rate, and bounce rate. Track these across every campaign and flow to see what's working and where value leaks: Metric What it tells you Open rate The share of recipients who open. Soft open rates usually point at the subject line or the sender name. Click-through rate (CTR) The share who click a link. Reads how well your content and CTA match what the subject line promised. Conversion rate The share who take the action you wanted, usually a purchase. The closest measure of business impact. Revenue per email Revenue generated divided by emails delivered. The truest read on what a single send is worth. Unsubscribe rate The share who opt out. A climbing rate signals fatigue or a mismatch with what people signed up for. Bounce rate The share that never reached an inbox. High bounces flag list-quality problems that drag down deliverability. Open rate. The share of recipients who open. Soft open rates usually point at the subject line or the sender name. Click-through rate (CTR). The share who click a link. This reads how well your content and CTA match what the subject line promised. Conversion rate. The share who take the action you wanted, usually a purchase. The closest measure of business impact. Revenue per email. Revenue generated divided by emails delivered. The truest read on what a single send is worth. Unsubscribe rate. The share who opt out. A climbing rate signals fatigue or a mismatch between what you send and what people signed up for. Bounce rate. The share that never reached an inbox. High bounces flag list-quality problems that drag down deliverability over time. Stage 5: Avoid the common pitfalls Most email programs stall for the same handful of reasons. Here's what each one looks like before it costs you: Emailing too much or too little. Over-send and people tune out or unsubscribe. Under-send and they forget you. Let engagement data set the cadence. Weak segmentation. Send the whole list one message and engagement drops while opt-outs climb. Flat subject lines. A dull subject line loses the open, and nothing downstream can win it back. Ignoring mobile. An email that breaks on a phone loses most of your audience before they read a word. Compliance missteps. Skipping consent or burying the unsubscribe link hurts deliverability and customer trust at once. Get the build, the measurement, and the guardrails working together and email stops being a series of one-off sends. title: How To Build a Successful Nurse Residency Program in 2026
summary: Learn how to build a successful nurse residency program, from curriculum design and competency tracking to ANCC PTAP accreditation readiness and nurse retention strategies.
body_text: KEY TAKEAWAYS: Build a structured nurse residency program with a clear curriculum. ​Validate clinical competency through assessments and checklists. ​​Use simulation to strengthen clinical decision-making. ​Develop communication, resilience, and emotional intelligence skills. ​Support new nurses through mentorship and preceptor guidance. ​Measure success through retention, competency, and engagement metrics Align the program with American Nurses Credentialing Center Practice Transition Accreditation Program (ANCC PTAP) accreditation standards. How nurse residency programs strengthen clinical readiness ‍ New graduate nurses face one of the steepest learning curves in any profession. They leave academic programs with strong foundational knowledge, but the realities of clinical practice require a different level of readiness — one that develops through time, support, and hands-on experience. A well-designed nurse residency program supports this growth. ​For healthcare organizations, the stakes couldn't be higher. Nurse turnover is expensive, patient safety depends on clinical confidence, and the nursing workforce itself is under sustained pressure. Nurse residency programs have emerged as one of the most effective ways to address all three challenges at once. ​This guide explains what a strong nurse residency program looks like in 2026, from curriculum design and competency development to accreditation readiness and long-term measurement. What is a nurse residency program? ​A nurse residency program is a structured, employer-based transition to practice program designed to support new graduate nurses as they move from academic education into clinical practice. Most programs run between 12 and 24 months, with 12 months being the standard recommended by the American Association of Colleges of Nursing (AACN) . ​The primary goals are to build clinical competence, reduce new-nurse turnover, and support patient safety. Rather than leaving new nurses to navigate unfamiliar environments on their own, residency programs provide a structured pathway with mentorship, skill development, and regular feedback built in from day one. Most programs run between 12 and 24 months, with 12 months being the standard recommended by the American Association of Colleges of Nursing (AACN). ​Why nurse residency programs matter more than ever in 2026 ​The nursing workforce is under pressure from multiple directions. Retaining experienced nurses, preparing new graduates, and maintaining safe staffing levels are all challenges that intersect directly with how well organizations support early-career nurses. Nurse residency programs address each of these challenges in meaningful ways. ​Addressing nurse turnover ​First-year nurse turnover remains one of the most costly workforce challenges in healthcare. According to NSI Nursing Solutions , the average cost of turnover for a bedside registered nurse now exceeds $60,000. However, nurse residency programs are consistently associated with lower first-year attrition, giving organizations a concrete way to protect their workforce investment. ​The average cost of turnover for a bedside RN now exceeds $60,000, but nurse residency programs are associated with lower first-year turnover. ​Building clinical confidence ​New graduates often report feeling underprepared for the realities of clinical practice. A structured transition to practice program addresses this directly by pairing progressive learning plans with hands-on experience, simulation, and regular competency assessments. ​Supporting patient safety ​Clinical errors are more likely when nurses feel uncertain or lack sufficient support. Research from the National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN) has linked structured transition-to-practice programs to improved patient safety outcomes, making residency programs a quality-of-care issue, not just a workforce one. ​Preparing the future nursing workforce ​The nursing profession is facing a generational shift. As experienced nurses retire, organizations need a reliable pipeline of prepared, confident clinicians. Nurse residency programs build that pipeline in a structured, consistent way rather than leaving new-nurse readiness to chance. ​The essential components of a successful nurse residency program ​Structured residency curriculum ​A strong nurse residency curriculum goes beyond orientation checklists. It includes core clinical topics applicable to all new nurses, specialty learning tracks for units like ICU, emergency, or perioperative care, and progressive learning plans that build complexity over time. The goal is a logical progression in which each stage builds the skills and confidence nurses need for the next. ​Competency development ​Clinical competency validation is the backbone of any effective nurse residency program. Skills assessments and competency checklists give educators and leaders a clear picture of where each nurse stands, and where additional support is needed. HealthStream's Competency Suite supports this process by enabling organizations to standardize competency tracking, manage checklists, and maintain documentation in one place — making it easier to identify gaps before they affect patient care. ​Simulation and scenario-based learning ​Realistic patient scenarios allow new nurses to practice critical thinking and clinical decision-making in a safe environment. Simulation gives learners a safe space to make mistakes, reflect on their decisions, and improve — without risk to patients. Organizations that invest in scenario-based learning report stronger clinical confidence among residency graduates. ​Communication and emotional intelligence ​Technical skills alone don't determine a nurse's effectiveness. Team communication, conflict resolution, patient communication, resilience, and self-awareness all shape how new nurses perform under pressure. A well-rounded nurse residency program incorporates these skills deliberately, rather than assuming they'll develop on their own. ​Mentorship and preceptor support ​Preceptors are among the most important resources a new nurse has. Structured preceptor training, clear coaching frameworks, and regular feedback loops give preceptors the tools they need to support residents effectively. Peer support structures also matter, as new nurses benefit from connecting with others navigating similar challenges. ​Measuring nurse residency program success ​Measuring program outcomes is essential to evaluating and improving a nurse residency program. The following indicators give organizations a reliable picture of program effectiveness. ​Nurse confidence surveys ​Regular confidence surveys track how new nurses feel about their clinical readiness over time. Trends across cohorts can reveal gaps in the curriculum or areas where simulation or mentorship could be strengthened. ​Retention rates ​First-year and second-year retention rates are among the clearest indicators of program impact. Organizations should track retention by unit, specialty, and cohort to identify patterns. ​Competency achievement ​Tracking the percentage of residents who meet competency benchmarks on schedule, and those who require remediation, helps educators refine learning plans and allocate support resources appropriately. ​ ​Engagement metrics ​Participation rates, assessment completion, and learning activity engagement all signal how invested residents are in the program. Low engagement often points to content, scheduling, or support issues worth addressing. ​Program dashboards and reporting ​Centralizing program data in a reporting dashboard makes it easier for nurse leaders to see the full picture and make informed decisions. HealthStream's Competency Suite supports this with reporting tools that consolidate competency data, assessment results, and completion rates across departments and specialties. ​ Preparing for ANCC PTAP and Magnet recognition ​The ANCC Practice Transition Accreditation Program provides a formal framework for evaluating and recognizing transition to practice programs. Achieving PTAP accreditation signals a meaningful commitment to new-nurse development and is closely linked to Magnet recognition. ​Accreditation readiness requires consistent documentation, organized evidence collection, and a culture of continuous improvement. Organizations that use structured tools to manage competency records and program data are better positioned to meet these requirements without scrambling to compile evidence at audit time. ​Common challenges when building a nurse residency program ​Even well-resourced organizations run into predictable obstacles: ​Limited educator resources: Nursing professional development practitioners are stretched thin. Programs that rely too heavily on a single educator or department are vulnerable to gaps. ​Inconsistent curriculum: Without standardization, program quality varies across units, shifts, and cohorts. ‍ ​Tracking competency across specialties: Managing competency data for nurses in different units often means having to work across disconnected systems. ‍ ​Measuring outcomes: Many organizations track completion rates while failing to measure other critical measures, including clinical confidence, retention, or patient outcomes. ‍ Administrative burden: Documentation and reporting requirements can consume significant time if not supported by the right tools. ​Recognizing these challenges early makes it easier to build a program designed to address them from the start. ​Best practices for launching or improving your program ​Use this checklist as a practical starting point for building or strengthening a nurse residency program: ​ Step 1: Establish clear, measurable learning objectives for each program phase ‍ Step 2: Standardize the curriculum across units and specialties ‍ Step 3: Incorporate simulation and scenario-based learning into the core program ‍ Step 4: Measure both confidence and clinical competency at regular intervals ‍ Step 5: Use data to identify gaps and continuously improve outcomes ‍ Step 6: Build structured mentorship opportunities with trained preceptors ‍ Step 7: Align program design and documentation with ANCC PTAP standards ‍ Step 8: Evaluate program performance at the end of each cohort and adjust accordingly ​ ​FAQs ​How long should a nurse residency program last? ‍ Most accreditation bodies, including the ANCC and AACN, recommend a minimum of 12 months. Some specialty areas, such as critical care or perioperative nursing, may benefit from longer programs of up to 24 months. ​What should be included in a nurse residency curriculum? ‍ A complete nurse residency curriculum includes core clinical content, specialty learning tracks, simulation-based learning, communication and emotional intelligence development, competency assessments, and structured mentorship. ​How do nurse residency programs improve retention? By building clinical confidence and providing structured support during the most vulnerable period of a nurse's career, nurse residency programs reduce the isolation and uncertainty that often drive early turnover. ​What is ANCC PTAP? The ANCC PTAP is a formal accreditation pathway that recognizes healthcare organizations for the quality of their transition to practice programs. It provides a structured framework for program design, documentation, and continuous improvement. ​ How do you measure the success of a nurse residency program? ‍ Key metrics include nurse confidence survey results, first-year and second-year retention rates, competency achievement rates, engagement with program activities, and overall program completion. Reporting dashboards help consolidate these data points for ongoing review. ​What is the difference between nurse orientation and a residency program? Nurse orientation is typically a brief, compliance-focused introduction to an organization's policies and procedures. A nurse residency program is a longer, structured developmental experience that builds clinical competence, professional identity, and long-term readiness for practice.

title: The Mayflower Update
summary: A new dawn for Bean Farmers.
body_text: On Season 6074, as the early dawn light broke across the rolling fields, the Farmers of Beanstalk gathered on the Mayflower, their trusty vessel, ready to set sail towards a new horizon. They had weathered many storms and worked hard to tend to their recovered crops, but they knew that in order to grow and thrive, they needed to adapt and evolve. Today, Beanstalk Farms is excited to announce the Mayflower Update and an anticipated launch timeline. Note: BIP-34 Sunrise Improvements and BIP-35: Stalk Delegation and Process Amendments were proposed today! The Mayflower Update consists of three major changes that will significantly improve the way the Beanstalk community experiences farming: (1) Sunrise Improvements, (2) Silo V3 and (3) Basin. Sunrise Improvements Today, the Sunrise Improvements BIP is live for voting . The Sunrise Improvements upgrade is primarily composed of 2 changes: Morning Auction When the Bean price is above peg, Beanstalk still issues Soil in order to measure demand for Soil (and consequently adjust the Temperature). However, during times of short-term excess demand for Soil, Beanstalk pays significantly more in Pods than is necessary to attract creditors. During the Morning of each Season (the first 5 minutes, or 25 blocks), the Temperature offered by Beanstalk is dynamic. Each Morning, the offered Temperature ramps from 1% to 100% of the maximum Temperature. The Morning Auction should reduce unnecessary Pod issuance, which should improve Beanstalk’s creditworthiness as a borrower. In addition, maximizing Beans borrowed for a given Pod issuance improves Beanstalk’s efficiency. Here's a preview of the new Field page in the Beanstalk UI: Sunrise Incentive Adjustment Beanstalk updates its monetary policy every Season, which occurs upon a successful call of the sunrise function. It costs gas to call the sunrise function and Beanstalk often overpays in Beans to incentivize users to call it. The Sunrise Incentive Adjustment upgrade makes it such that how much Beanstalk pays for incentivization of the sunrise function takes into account Ethereum network conditions (i.e., current gas costs) and Beanstalk economic conditions (i.e., the Bean price). Reducing unnecessary Bean issuance in the sunrise incentive reward should reduce sell pressure on Beans. Silo V3 The Silo V3 upgrade introduces multiple composability and UX improvements to the Silo, one of the core components of Beanstalk. Removal of the Withdrawal Timer When Beanstalk was launched in August 2021, Farmers had to wait 24 Seasons before being able to claim Withdrawn assets from the Silo. This lockup period likely served Beanstalk well during its infancy stage. Now that Beanstalk is more established, and more participants understand the incentives of the Stalk System, it has become clear that the Withdrawal timer is an economic inefficiency that creates a supply overhang when there are Withdrawn assets. Since Replant, the Withdrawal timer has lasted until the remainder of the current Season. Now that the Withdrawal timer is being removed, Bean seigniorage will be distributed based on a time-weighted average, rather than based Stalk at the end of the Season. Distributing seigniorage this way eliminates the profit of a potential attack where a user deposits assets in the Silo, calls sunrise , earns Bean seigniorage and withdraws the assets all in a single transaction while retaining Bean exposure for zero blocks. Examples of developments that become possible after the removal of the Withdrawal timer include the redemption of Roots for Circulating Beans in a single transaction, the ability to order Pods on the Market with Deposits, etc. Tokenization of Deposits as ERC-1155s Making the positive carry of holding Beans usable in DeFi is critical to the success of Beanstalk. In practice, this means facilitating economic activity in Silo Deposits, given that it is Deposits that earn Bean inflation (and not Beans that are held outside the Silo). To that end, tokenizing Deposits and having them conform to an established ERC standard like ERC-1155 is a necessary step in this direction. This will immediately provide utility in the form of a permissionless market for Deposits on existing infrastructure like OpenSea. Dynamic Seeds per BDV Currently, there is no straightforward way to change the Seeds per BDV rewards for a given Silo Deposit type. After Silo V3, it will be possible for the DAO to adjust the Seeds reward for a given whistlisted asset via BIP. This serves as the technical foundation for a future Gauge System where the DAO can express preferences that lead to Stalk and Seed rewards for various whitelisted assets changing in real time. Unripe Seeds Parity Currently, Unripe Bean Deposits receive 2 Seeds per BDV and Unripe BEAN:3CRV LP Deposits receive 4 Seeds per BDV. Most Bean liquidity is underlying Unripe LP, but converting to Unripe Beans results in a loss of Seeds. This seems to be one of the primary reasons for why a significant amount of Unripe LP remains in the Silo despite the opportunity to convert to Unripe Beans to arbitrage the Bean price. Changing the Seed rewards for both Unripe assets to the same value would remove a significant cost to converting from Unripe LP to Unripe Beans. This may result in more conversions, which would have a significant effect on peg maintenance. A DAO vote is likely in order to determine what the exact Seeds per BDV values for Unripe Beans and Unripe BEAN:3CRV LP should be set to in Silo V3. Basin Liquidity pools on the upcoming DEX are known as Wells, but the overall DEX architecture is known as Basin. Give the new Basin Twitter account a follow. There are a number of problems with current implementations of AMMs on Ethereum. In a post-Merge environment, existing on-chain AMMs are not multi-block MEV resistant. Given that Beanstalk needs to price Beans against other assets (on-chain) and that the goal of Beanstalk is to be as censorship and manipulation resistant as possible, multi-block MEV is an attack vector that should be addressed. Additionally, most AMMs in DeFi are generally not designed to be composable and have little flexibility in allowing developers customize their liquidity pool implementation. Trading fees, pricing functions, and price oracles are embedded and cannot be customized independently. Basin aims to solve these problems: Pumps, the oracles of the Basin DEX are composable and customizable by design. The first implementation developed by Beanstalk Farms provides the first multi-block MEV resistant oracle implementation on the Ethereum network. Developers can utilize the work of other ecosystem contributors and the Beanstalk DAO who develop, audit and deploy custom pricing functions, Pump implementations, and even new pool factory contracts. The composability of Basin also allows for the deployment of Wells with zero trading fees. Providing liquidity to Wells which do not collect trading fees can be incentivized via protocol-native incentives, such as whitelisting the Well LP token in the Silo. See Publius' Worthless Tech and Beanstalk Development Update writeups for a deep-dive. Basin Integration Launching Basin in a way that Beanstalk directly benefits from requires a BIP that integrates the two protocols. Integrating the two protocols means: Support for Beanstalk to compute the BDV of a given Well LP token in order to reward a corresponding amount of Stalk and Seeds upon Deposit in the Silo; Conversions to and from Beans and the Well LP token (at minimum); Support for Beanstalk to read how far above or below peg the Bean price is in a Well, such that Beanstalk can mint Beans/Soil accordingly; and Whitelisting the BEAN:ETH Well LP token. Anticipated Mayflower Timeline Last updated May 24, 2023. Late April BIP-34: Sunrise Improvements Voting Period begins BIP-35: Stalk Delegation and Process Amendments Voting Period begins Halborn and Cyfrin audits of Basin end Silo V3 audit begins Early May BIP-34 and BIP-35 Voting Periods end Basin Integration audit starts Late May Fix review for Halborn and Cyfrin audits of Basin end Early June Silo V3 audit ends Code4rena audit of Basin begins and ends Mid June BIP-36: Silo V3 Voting Period begins Late June Basin Integration audit ends BIP-36 Voting Period ends Unripe Seeds parity is launched Early July The Basin DEX and a BEAN:ETH Well is deployed BIP-37: Basin Integration Voting Period begins Mid July BIP-37 Voting Period ends BEAN:ETH Well becomes whitelisted in the Silo
